round1.proposed_rule: Met only if the report names, for each data source used for development or evaluation, a specific design. This means either a temporal design (e.g. cross-sectional; cohort, longitudinal or panel with follow-up) or a sampling design (e.g. complex, multistage, stratified or cluster probability sampling; use of survey sampling weights). General descriptors on their own do not meet it. These include 'survey', 'nationally representative', 'population-based', 'publicly available' and 'observational study'; 'observational study' describes the analysis, not the data source. If a design is stated for only some of the sources, the item is not_met, and the rationale names the source that lacks one. If two places give contradictory designs for the same source (e.g. cross-sectional without follow-up vs panel data), the item is still met, with inconsistency present.

Code met only when a specific study or sampling design is explicitly described for every data source used for model development or evaluation; otherwise code not_met. A generic survey description, national representativeness, or calling the analysis observational alone is insufficient; an explicitly described cohort or participant follow-up qualifies for that source. Both response codes have status reported. Apply the existing inconsistency rule separately: contradictory design statements about the same source under the same conditions give inconsistency present, without changing status or negating that its design was stated.

Not met if the only information is the total number analysed, eligibility or inclusion criteria (e.g. an adult age limit), the outcome class counts or the outcome-score distribution. Record as inconsistency any participant counts or characteristics that the report prints differently for the same group, following the general inconsistency rule.

Code met when the report gives a descriptive summary of at least one non-outcome characteristic of the analysed participants, such as a sex count/proportion or an age summary; text, tables and figures qualify. No characteristics table, multiple characteristics or outcome prevalence is required, and either response code has status reported. Assess inconsistency separately under the existing rule: present requires two supported statements contradicting the same fact, object and condition; uncertain requires potentially conflicting statements whose objects cannot be matched; otherwise use none. Missing source text, unstated denominators, category completeness, row labels or figure membership must not be inferred to establish a contradiction.

round1.proposed_rule: For this item, inconsistency concerns only the printed performance estimates of the final or main model(s). Contradictions about other facts are recorded in their own items, not here. Such facts include which comparators were used, claims about models with no printed results, and the same number appearing in different cells. Record present only when both places state the same model, the same metric and the same dataset or sample (named in the text itself or in its paragraph, heading or the table it cites) and give different values. If one place does not name the metric or the dataset or sample, record uncertain; do not infer it from matching numbers. Values printed under different metric names (e.g. accuracy vs correct proportion) are different statistics unless the report says they are the same, so record none. Do not use your own arithmetic to decide whether they are the same.

Numerical performance estimates for the final or main model(s) meet this requirement: status reported, value met. Inconsistency never changes that result. Record inconsistency present only when cited statements contradict the same fact for the same model, metric, dataset and condition; use uncertain when a possible contradiction cannot be resolved because those identities or conditions are unclear, and none when no contradiction is found. Missing comparator results do not themselves contradict a comparison claim. Use only supplied evidence: numerical resemblance or arithmetic equality does not establish a metric’s identity, and uncited or absent text cannot establish a contradiction.

round1.proposed_rule: Met only if every split or resampling that produces the reported performance estimates (internal or external evaluation) has its defining details printed. For a data split, that means the proportion or the size of each set. For cross-validation, the number of folds, plus the number of repetitions if it was repeated. For bootstrap, the number of replicates. If any of these is missing for an evaluation split or resampling, the code is not_met. Fold counts or other details given only for resampling used in tuning, predictor selection, threshold selection, resampling for class imbalance or recalibration do not make up for missing details of the evaluation split. If the report describes no split and no resampling of any kind (the model is fitted and described on the whole sample only), the requirement has no object: status not_applicable (NA), not not_met.

Code met when at least one split or resampling procedure has a stated implementation detail, such as a split proportion, fold count or repetition count; include resampling for tuning or recalibration, and do not require details for every procedure. An explicit statement that no splitting or resampling was done meets the reporting requirement; both met and not_met have status reported and kind judged. Assess inconsistency separately using the existing same-object, same-condition rule: do not assume participant subsets are disjoint when observations were split, and use uncertain for potentially conflicting counts whose identity as the same exhaustive partition cannot be established.

round1.proposed_rule: Met when the report (text or figure) gives the source count, the analysed-sample count and a count for every exclusion step it presents between them (the number excluded or remaining). Inconsistency for the flow: present only when two places give different counts, or criteria that cannot both be true, for the same step. A step named in one place and left out of another, or a wrong figure cross-reference, is none (note it in the rationale). Uncertain when counts fail to add up only if figure numbers are matched to boxes or steps in a way the input does not print, or when the same step is given reasons naming different data and the report does not show whether they describe the same exclusion.

Code met when printed source and analysed-sample counts are linked by stated selection criteria, with a remaining or excluded count for every explicitly distinguished intermediate selection stage.
